name: weight-left
description: Contrapposto with the weight over the left leg. What a weight shift settles into.
notes: Contrapposto is not a lean. It is four things happening at once, and if any one is missing the figure reads as tipping over rather than resting: the pelvis translates over the stance foot, the stance-side iliac crest rises, the lumbar spine bends back the other way to bring the head over the support, and the shoulder line ends up tilted OPPOSITE to the hip line.

That last part is the one most often got backwards. Weight on the left leg raises the LEFT hip and drops the LEFT shoulder. The two lines converge on the weighted side and diverge on the free side, and it is that divergence — a long open flank on one side and a short compressed one on the other — that produces the S every life class teaches. Tilt them the same way and the figure looks braced, not resting. Measured here: hip line +5.5 degrees, shoulder line -3.0.

FEET STAY PLANTED. There is no foot IK behind this, so the legs are counter-rotated by hand. The pelvis rolls 5.5 degrees and travels 40 mm; a thigh that simply rode along would swing the stance foot more than 70 mm outward and lift it off the floor. Each thigh therefore carries roughly the negative of the pelvis roll plus whatever that leg is actually doing, and the measured foot and toe positions are the check — the stance foot lands within 5 mm of where relaxed-standing leaves it laterally, and both feet stay within about 20 mm fore and aft. That residue is deliberate rather than tolerated: a real weight shift does reposition the feet slightly, and pinning them exactly would need IK this does not have.

The free leg does what a free leg does: hip slightly flexed so the knee comes forward, knee softly bent to about 15 degrees, foot a little wider and turned out more than the stance foot. The stance leg is close to straight and close to vertical under the pelvis, which is what carrying the load looks like.

THE FREE KNEE COMES ACROSS, and this is the part the pose was missing for two rounds. With the hip carried by the pelvis and the foot pinned to the floor, the knee is the ONLY thing on a leg that can move, and it can only move on a circle: the intersection of a sphere of radius L1 about the hip with a sphere of radius L2 about the ankle. That circle's radius is (L1.L2/D).sin(knee flexion), so it is 23.8 mm on this figure's near-straight stance leg and 51.5 mm on its free leg at 14.76 degrees of flexion. A LOADED LIMB IS A COLUMN AND HAS NO ARTICULATION TO SPEND — that is what carrying a body means — and every millimetre the lower body has is on the free side. The pose used to spend none of it: both legs were counter-rotated by the same amount (-8.5 and -9.0 degrees of adduction against relaxed-standing, a differential of half a degree) so the leg pair rotated in COMMON MODE, which is by construction the shape-preserving mode. A blind visual judge measured the result at 0.81 px of shape change against 8.2 px of translation, with the two thigh edges correlated at r = 0.995, and called it a rigid cut-out sliding sideways.

So the free limb is swivelled 16 degrees about its own hip-to-ankle axis. The hip is the pivot, the ankle is ON the axis, and the leg turns as a rigid body — measured: the ankle moves 0.058 mm, the toe 0.66 mm, and knee flexion is 14.76 degrees before and after. The knee travels 14.3 mm toward the midline, which takes the inter-thigh gap at full blend from 26.92 px to 18.23 px at the framing alive.js?frame=body uses, against 27.27 px in relaxed-standing. That is 9.04 px of shape change where the pose used to deliver 0.35 px.

The swivel drags the foot round with it, and that is taken back below the knee rather than left to splay the stance out: 9 degrees as tibial axial rotation about the knee-to-ankle axis, which is what a knee flexed this far permits and which moves neither the knee nor the ankle, and the remaining 6.5 degrees as a foot yaw about the rig's vertical through the ankle — the one rotation that maps the floor plane to itself and therefore cannot tilt or lift the sole. Measured after: heel centres 169.9 mm and included foot angle 14.81 degrees, against 169.8 and 14.76 before, so the stance this pose is solved to is untouched.

ARMS. The stance-side hip juts out, so the arm on that side hangs 2 degrees further out to clear it and the free-side arm hangs 2 degrees closer in. Everything else about the arms and hands is relaxed-standing unchanged — a weight shift is a pelvis and spine event, and animating the fingers along with it would read as a whole-body flinch.

STANCE WIDTH. This pose carries the same narrowing relaxed-standing does — heel centres at McIlroy and Maki's preferred 0.17 m rather than the bind pose's 0.38 m; see that file's notes for the source and the solve. The SAME adduction and external rotation are added here as there, deliberately: Sway blends the difference between relaxed-standing and this pose, so one common delta leaves every authored contrapposto angle exactly as it was drawn. Only the pelvis height is re-solved, against the mean of the two ankles. Measured after: heel centres 169.8 mm, included angle 14.76 degrees, outer-to-outer 298.1 mm.

hips.why: z: +5.5 raises the left (stance) crest — a positive roll about the forward axis lifts everything on the +X side. y: -2 takes the stance side very slightly back, which is the transverse component of a real weight shift.

spine.why: The lumbar counter-bend, and the largest single number in the pose. It over-corrects the pelvis's 5.5 degrees so the net trunk lean ends up toward the stance side rather than away from it.

chest.why: Carries the bend up. Sharing it across three spine bones is what makes a curve rather than a hinge.

upperChest.why: Turns the curve back — the top of the S. Accumulated roll at the chest lands near -3 degrees, which is what tips the shoulder line opposite to the hip line.

neck.why: Brings the head back toward vertical.

head.why: Levels the eyes. A contrapposto with a tilted horizon reads as a stumble.

leftShoulder.why: As relaxed-standing. The shoulder drop on this side comes from the spine, not from the clavicle.

leftUpperArm.why: Two degrees less adduction than relaxed-standing: the stance hip juts out under this arm and the arm has to clear it.

rightUpperArm.why: Two degrees more adduction: nothing under this arm to clear, and the free-side flank is the long one.

leftUpperLeg.why: Stance leg. Against relaxed-standing's [0, 9.56, -5.29] this is +2.0 of external rotation and -8.5 of adduction: the -8.5 undoes the pelvis's +5.5 roll and adds three degrees on top, which is what keeps the planted foot planted while the pelvis travels 40 mm over it. The absolute numbers carry the narrowed stance; the DELTA from relaxed-standing is the contrapposto and is unchanged.

leftLowerLeg.why: The stance knee stays where the bind pose has it. A knee carrying the load is close to straight.

leftFoot.why: The stance foot's counter-rotation for the narrowed stance; see relaxed-standing.

rightUpperLeg.why: Free leg, SWIVELLED. The pre-swivel angles were [-4, -7.06, 0.94]: +2.0 of external rotation and -9.0 of adduction against relaxed-standing's [0, -9.06, 9.94], undoing the pelvis roll so the free foot lands slightly wider, with x: -4 flexing the hip to send the knee forward — a bone pointing DOWN moves backward under a positive x rotation, which is the sign trap in this whole file. These angles are that pose turned a further 16 degrees about the hip-to-ankle axis, which is why y swings so far: a swivel about a near-vertical axis reads mostly as femoral axial rotation. See the notes — the whole of it moves the knee 14.3 mm and nothing else.

rightLowerLeg.why: Free knee softly flexed to 14.8 degrees total — unchanged by the swivel, which turns the leg as a rigid body. The y term is 9 degrees of tibial axial rotation about the knee-to-ankle axis, taking back the larger half of the foot rotation the swivel would otherwise have handed to the floor. It moves neither the knee nor the ankle: both are on that axis.

rightFoot.why: Levels the sole back toward the floor after the shank has swung, carries the narrowed stance's counter-rotation, and absorbs the last 6.5 degrees of the swivel as a yaw about the rig's vertical. A yaw maps the floor plane to itself, so the sole cannot tilt or lift no matter how large it gets — which is the same argument Sway's FREE_FOOT_YAW_RELEASE makes for letting a free foot turn under an unloading leg.
